data.title: We Don’t Think MAKUS' (KOSDAQ:093520) Earnings Should Make Shareholders Too Comfortable
data.description:
Solid profit numbers didn't seem to be enough to please MAKUS Inc.'s (KOSDAQ:093520) shareholders. Our analysis has found some concerning factors which weaken the profit's foundation.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

A Closer Look At MAKUS' Earnings

One key financial ratio used to measure how well a company converts its profit to free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio. To get the accrual ratio we first subtract FCF from profit for a period, and then divide that number by the average operating assets for the period. You could think of the accrual ratio from cashflow as the 'non-FCF profit ratio'.

Therefore, it's actually considered a good thing when a company has a negative accrual ratio, but a bad thing if its accrual ratio is positive. While it's not a problem to have a positive accrual ratio, indicating a certain level of non-cash profits, a high accrual ratio is arguably a bad thing, because it indicates paper profits are not matched by cash flow. Notably, there is some academic evidence that suggests that a high accrual ratio is a bad sign for near-term profits, generally speaking.

MAKUS has an accrual ratio of 1.33 for the year to September 2026. Statistically speaking, that's a real negative for future earnings. To wit, the company did not generate one whit of free cashflow in that time. In the last twelve months it actually had negative free cash flow, with an outflow of ₩26b despite its profit of ₩35.1b, mentioned above. We saw that FCF was ₩85b a year ago though, so MAKUS has at least been able to generate positive FCF in the past. Having said that, there is more to the story. The accrual ratio is reflecting the impact of unusual items on statutory profit, at least in part. The good news for shareholders is that MAKUS' accrual ratio was much better last year, so this year's poor reading might simply be a case of a short term mismatch between profit and FCF. Shareholders should look for improved cashflow relative to profit in the current year, if that is indeed the case.

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

How Do Unusual Items Influence Profit?

The fact that the company had unusual items boosting profit by ₩6.0b, in the last year, probably goes some way to explain why its accrual ratio was so weak. While it's always nice to have higher profit, a large contribution from unusual items sometimes dampens our enthusiasm. We ran the numbers on most publicly listed companies worldwide, and it's very common for unusual items to be once-off in nature. And that's as you'd expect, given these boosts are described as 'unusual'. Assuming those unusual items don't show up again in the current year, we'd thus expect profit to be weaker next year (in the absence of business growth, that is).

Our Take On MAKUS' Profit Performance

Summing up, MAKUS received a nice boost to profit from unusual items, but could not match its paper profit with free cash flow. Considering all this we'd argue MAKUS' profits probably give an overly generous impression of its sustainable level of profitability. In light of this, if you'd like to do more analysis on the company, it's vital to be informed of the risks involved. To that end, you should learn about the 2 warning signs we've spotted with MAKUS (including 1 which shouldn't be ignored).

data.title: Here's Why We're Wary Of Buying Inter Action's (TSE:7725) For Its Upcoming Dividend
data.description:
It looks like Inter Action Corporation (TSE:7725) is about to go ex-dividend in the next four days. The ex-dividend date is commonly two business days before the record date, which is the cut-off date for shareholders to be present on the company's books to be eligible for a dividend payment. The ex-dividend date is an important date to be aware of as any purchase of the stock made on or after this date might mean a late settlement that doesn't show on the record date. This means that investors who purchase Inter Action's shares on or after the 27th of November will not receive the dividend, which will be paid on the 16th of February.

The company's next dividend payment will be JP¥10.00 per share, on the back of last year when the company paid a total of JP¥45.00 to shareholders. Based on the last year's worth of payments, Inter Action has a trailing yield of 3.0% on the current stock price of JP¥1482.00. Dividends are an important source of income to many shareholders, but the health of the business is crucial to maintaining those dividends. That's why we should always check whether the dividend payments appear sustainable, and if the company is growing.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

If a company pays out more in dividends than it earned, then the dividend might become unsustainable - hardly an ideal situation. Inter Action distributed an unsustainably high 111% of its profit as dividends to shareholders last year. Without extenuating circumstances, we'd consider the dividend at risk of a cut. Yet cash flows are even more important than profits for assessing a dividend, so we need to see if the company generated enough cash to pay its distribution. Thankfully its dividend payments took up just 42% of the free cash flow it generated, which is a comfortable payout ratio.

It's good to see that while Inter Action's dividends were not covered by profits, at least they are affordable from a cash perspective. Still, if the company repeatedly paid a dividend greater than its profits, we'd be concerned. Very few companies are able to sustainably pay dividends larger than their reported earnings.

Check out our latest analysis for Inter Action

Click here to see how much of its profit Inter Action paid out over the last 12 months.

Have Earnings And Dividends Been Growing?

When earnings decline, dividend companies become much harder to analyse and own safely. If earnings decline and the company is forced to cut its dividend, investors could watch the value of their investment go up in smoke. Readers will understand then, why we're concerned to see Inter Action's earnings per share have dropped 18% a year over the past five years. When earnings per share fall, the maximum amount of dividends that can be paid also falls.

Many investors will assess a company's dividend performance by evaluating how much the dividend payments have changed over time. In the last 10 years, Inter Action has lifted its dividend by approximately 22% a year on average. The only way to pay higher dividends when earnings are shrinking is either to pay out a larger percentage of profits, spend cash from the balance sheet, or borrow the money. Inter Action is already paying out a high percentage of its income, so without earnings growth, we're doubtful of whether this dividend will grow much in the future.

Final Takeaway

From a dividend perspective, should investors buy or avoid Inter Action? It's not a great combination to see a company with earnings in decline and paying out 111% of its profits, which could imply the dividend may be at risk of being cut in the future. However, the cash payout ratio was much lower - good news from a dividend perspective - which makes us wonder why there is such a mis-match between income and cashflow. It's not the most attractive proposition from a dividend perspective, and we'd probably give this one a miss for now.

So if you're still interested in Inter Action despite it's poor dividend qualities, you should be well informed on some of the risks facing this stock. Every company has risks, and we've spotted 3 warning signs for Inter Action you should know about.

data.title: Caught Out By Vonovia's Fall? Here's What The Bears Saw
data.description:

Holding Vonovia over the past year would have meant a 31.3% loss, including dividends. Those Q1 headlines about higher group adjusted EBITDA and easing leverage then meet later news of profit falling as a prior tax windfall disappeared. The Two Stories Vonovia Investors Were Weighing

The shares cost €25.9 at the start of the period, and anyone looking at Vonovia then had to choose between two very different stories about what came next.

On the upbeat side, one scenario pointed to a Fair Value of €34.88, essentially a notional price if service expansion and photovoltaic projects did lift non rental EBITDA and support the plan for adjusted rental EBITDA to compound at 4%.

A more cautious view held that rising European rates and tighter rules would bite harder, with a Fair Value of €24 implying pressure if higher refinancing costs met stricter rent controls and heavy energy efficiency capex.

What The Evidence Did To The Vonovia Argument

The clearest test came from Vonovia’s Q3 2026 figures. Total revenue of €1,429.2m sat slightly below the prior €1,438m, while net income excluding extra items fell from €2,284.5m to €232m. That weak profitability picture challenged the bullish idea that EBITDA growth from services and photovoltaics would quickly translate into stronger net earnings. Overall, the evidence cut both ways.

The key assumption here was that higher Rental and Value-add EBITDA would reliably flow through to bottom line progress. For any other property group, it would be important to watch net income and leverage alongside segment EBITDA before relying on a similar story.

The core consideration is whether German housing demand remains tight enough for large residential owners such as Vonovia to continue benefiting from what local investors refer to as “golden concrete”. A buyer today would need to believe that this structural housing pressure endures over many years.

  • Chief executive Elon Musk described the new FSD v15 interface as "mind-bending," highlighting a reality rendering visualization for drivers.
  • The upgraded visualization will be available to vehicles equipped with Tesla's Hardware 4 platform, limiting access for older models.
  • The FSD v15 wide release with the new reality rendering interface is a key product move that needs weighing against the rest of the picture. Check out 3 warning signs that Tesla investors should know about.

This push toward more advanced in-car autonomy software is not limited to Tesla, so it is worth comparing against peers exposed to the same AI infrastructure trend through 52 AI infrastructure stocks.

Tesla now pitches FSD as a core software layer on top of its electric vehicles and energy products, which puts its auto business in a different bucket from traditional car makers that focus mainly on hardware. This software heavy approach means feature releases like v15 can matter for how you think about the broader ecosystem, not just the driving experience.

1 thing going right for Tesla that this headline doesn't cover.

Does FSD v15 move Tesla closer to the software-first story or just refresh the paint?

Tesla’s Narrative treats Full Self-Driving and autonomy services as the key shift that turns an EV maker into a software and robotics platform. A wide FSD v15 rollout with a reality-rendering UI plugs directly into that bet that recurring autonomy revenue matters more than metal.

"The rapid rollout and scaling of Tesla's robotaxi and autonomous ride-hailing services... keeps the prospect of a larger, software heavy revenue mix and higher net margins in play..."

See how the full story points towards a $418 fair value for Tesla.

This FSD v15 release leans into exactly the catalyst analysts are watching, higher FSD subscription adoption and more autonomy usage per vehicle. It still has to be weighed against the heavy capital spend on AI chips, Cybercab and Optimus that has already pushed free cash flow negative, a risk already flagged in the Narrative.

Limiting the new interface to Hardware 4 cars may support the premium, software-first positioning against players like Mercedes and XPeng, but it also narrows the immediate monetisation base. For investors, the same update can either look like proof that Tesla is building the autonomy stack it needs or just another costly feature layered onto a stretched capex plan.

Which side you lean toward depends less on this specific FSD upgrade and more on the Narrative you hold about how quickly Tesla can turn autonomy spending into durable, high-margin software income.

data.title: How AI Network Tools Will Impact T Mobile Stock Investors
data.description:
• T-Mobile US recently highlighted new AI-powered AutoPilot and Dynamic CX tools for its 5G network, a Formula 1 Las Vegas deployment showcasing advanced 5G use cases, and reported work on T-Select prepaid plans aimed at more price sensitive users.
  • These moves tie network automation, event-grade 5G capabilities and fresh prepaid offers together, which points to T-Mobile US pushing both premium experiences and value focused segments while satellite players such as SpaceX signal future competitive pressure.
  • We will now look at how T-Mobile US's AI driven network management push could influence the broader investment narrative for the business.
Spot emerging telecom contenders by scanning the curated 40 high quality undervalued stocks, which may echo T-Mobile US' push into AI managed networks and premium event grade 5G experiences.

T-Mobile US Investment Narrative Recap

To own T-Mobile US, you need to believe the business can keep turning network and AI spending into higher value postpaid, broadband and adjacent revenue, while holding churn in check. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St leans on this, as well as guided adjusted free cash flow of about US$18.4b to US$18.8b in 2026. The short term swing factor is customer behavior as plan modernization and price increases roll through bills.

The biggest risk still sits with elevated churn and heavier promotional pressure as rivals and cable chase similar users. The Formula 1 deployment, AutoPilot tools and T-Select reports do not remove that churn and pricing risk, although they may help defend perceived network quality and broaden the funnel.

The most relevant recent update here is T-Mobile US rolling out AI powered AutoPilot and Dynamic CX across its 5G network. Those systems are designed to tune performance automatically and support reliability investments such as backup power and diversified transport. That operational focus directly supports the margin and service quality uplift that analysts build into earnings and free cash flow expectations.

If network automation and resilience work as intended at scale, including at demanding events like Formula 1 Las Vegas, they can reinforce the core catalyst of converting spectrum and 5G capacity into higher value postpaid and broadband revenue. Execution risk sits in whether these tools actually reduce care volumes and costs at the level implied in the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St, while competitive and regulatory pressures continue to build.

T-Mobile US' narrative projects US$105.5b revenue and US$18.2b earnings by 2029. This rests on 4.0% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase of about US$6.9b from the current US$11.3b level.

Exploring Other Perspectives

One alternate view focuses on prepaid and wholesale pressure rather than T-Mobile US network showpieces like the Formula 1 Las Vegas build. The most cautious analysts had been working off about US$102.2b of 2029 revenue and US$16.0b of earnings, and a lower 11.5x P/E. That mindset could shift if this type of AI managed 5G deployment changes how you see future mix and pricing power.
